source_text.body:
Reverse engineer AirPlay overnight
A user asked their agent to reverse engineer AirPlay overnight; it tried to verify the result by playing sound at max volume and listening through the laptop mic.
·
Nov 18, 2026
Done with a
custom-built or unnamed agent
What they did
Armin Ronacher asked his agent to reverse engineer AirPlay overnight. At 3 AM the agent decided the way to check its work was to play a sound in the living room and listen for it on the laptop microphone. To make it audible, it raised the volume to maximum.
How it went
The agent's verification plan woke Armin up. The post doesn't say whether the AirPlay reverse engineering succeeded or what it produced.
Worth knowing
An agent left running unattended can change real-world settings like speaker volume, so limit what it can control before leaving it overnight.
Try it yourself
with
Claude Code
Copy prompt
I want to reverse engineer [protocol or device, e.g. a smart speaker's streaming protocol] on this machine while I'm away. Capture traffic, read any public docs, and write a working proof-of-concept client in [language] in this folder, plus a notes file on what you learned. Verify it works in a safe way, keeping volume at a low level [e.g. 20%], and stop once a test succeeds or you've tried [number] approaches. Pause and ask me before installing anything system-wide or touching devices other than [my device].
Original source: https://bsky.app/profile/mitsuhiko.at/post/3n2mokm5eo22t
